newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy GDP seen growing in 2nd qtr - Isco institute.
newsitem.headline: Italy GDP seen growing in 2nd qtr - Isco institute.

text.p: Italy's gross domestic product (GDP) is likely to have grown in the second quarter of this year compared with the first quarter, state-funded economic research institute Isco said in a report on Thursday.
"Based on available data, second quarter GDP should have posted a considerable upswing over the first quarter and be enough to make up for preceding downturns," Isco said.
In the first quarter Italian GDP contracted by 0.4 percent year-on-year and slipped 0.2 percent from the fourth quarter of last year.

Isco said that in recent months there had emerged "clear signals of an improvement in the tone of economic activity" and that "the phase of stagnation which characterised 1996 and the start of 1997 can now be considered to be overcome".
The recovery in output should continue and consolidate in coming months, it added.
A Reuters quarterly poll of analysts earlier this month forecast on average growth of 1.0 percent in second-quarter GDP.
Isco said that the trend in industrial production, which grew in May for the fifth consecutive month, pointed to "further progress in June along with a considerable improvement in order books".
The survey, carried out at the start of July, confirmed both an upturn in foreign orders and clear progress in domestic orders.
An important factor underpinning the recovery, Isco added, was household demand, which had shown "appreciable dynamism" in the past few months. -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
